reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Mixing mTICI with eTICI or 2c grades.
name: Modified Treatment in Cerebral Ischaemia (mTICI) Grade

version.label: mTICI (consensus recommendations, Zaidat et al. 2013)
version.detail: Grades 0, 1, 2a, 2b, 3. Grade 2c and the eTICI scale are later versions and are not combined.

intendedPopulation: Patients after endovascular treatment for large vessel occlusion, graded on final angiography.

options.label: No perfusion
options.detail: No antegrade flow beyond the occlusion.

options.label: Minimal perfusion
options.detail: Contrast passes the occlusion with limited, slow distal branch filling and little perfusion.

options.label: Partial reperfusion (<50%)
options.detail: Antegrade reperfusion of less than half of the previously ischaemic territory.

options.label: Substantial reperfusion (≥50%)
options.detail: Antegrade reperfusion of more than half of the previously ischaemic territory.

options.label: Complete reperfusion
options.detail: Complete antegrade reperfusion with no visible occlusion in distal branches, at this assessment.

resultStates.label: No perfusion
resultStates.summary: No antegrade flow beyond the occlusion.
resultStates.detail: Assess further management according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

resultStates.label: Minimal perfusion
resultStates.summary: Contrast passes the occlusion with limited, slow distal branch filling and little perfusion.
resultStates.detail: Assess further management according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

resultStates.label: Partial reperfusion (<50%)
resultStates.summary: Antegrade reperfusion of less than half of the previously ischaemic territory.

resultStates.label: Substantial reperfusion (≥50%)
resultStates.summary: Antegrade reperfusion of more than half of the previously ischaemic territory.
resultStates.detail: mTICI 2b–3 is the usual definition of successful reperfusion in trials.

resultStates.label: Complete reperfusion
resultStates.summary: Complete antegrade reperfusion with no visible occlusion in distal branches, at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Final angiographic result; clinical outcome also depends on infarct core, time and collaterals.

clinicalContext.text: Standard endpoint for reperfusion after thrombectomy; mTICI 2b–3 defines successful reperfusion.

clinicalInsights.text: 2b spans 50–99%: later versions add 2c (near-complete) to separate these.

limitations.text: Visual estimate on angiography with moderate inter-rater agreement, especially between 2a and 2b.

limitations: Graded in the territory of the target occlusion only.

confounders.effect: Can hide or exaggerate perfusion defects.

guideSections.what: A five-level grade of reperfusion after thrombectomy.
guideSections.whenToUse: Reporting final angiographic results after endovascular stroke treatment.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess antegrade reperfusion of the previously ischaemic territory on final angiography in two projections; choose the grade.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A technical endpoint; correlate with imaging and clinical course.

sources.citation: Zaidat OO, Yoo AJ, Khatri P, et al. Recommendations on angiographic revascularization grading standards for acute ischemic stroke: a consensus statement. Stroke. 2013;44(9):2650-2663.
